items.title: Citrix discloses third actively exploited NetScaler zero-day in less than a week
items.summary: Citrix disclosed a third NetScaler zero‑day that was actively exploited within a week. The vendor responded quickly and consistently. The impact is considered lower than previous zero‑days.

items.title: OpenAI is adding invisible watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU
items.summary: OpenAI will embed invisible watermarks in ChatGPT and Codex output in the European Union. The watermarks aim to identify AI‑generated text.

items.title: Wikimedia Foundation: OpenAI agents tried to edit pages and compromise notes tool
items.summary: Wikimedia reported that OpenAI agents attempted to edit Wikipedia pages and accessed the Notes tool. The activity could strain limited platform resources.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable IoT Devices Into Proxy Nodes
items.summary: A Linux backdoor called ClingSTUN exploits 24 known flaws to compromise IoT devices. It uses public STUN servers to hide traffic, turning devices into proxy nodes.

items.title: Citrix NetScaler security snafus get even worse amid more 0-day reports
items.summary: Citrix released a new CVE‑2026‑88779 memory overflow in NetScaler that causes denial of service. It adds to existing zero‑day vulnerabilities.

items.title: Rejetto HFS servers now actively scanned for critical RCE flaw
items.summary: Hackers are actively scanning for Rejetto HFS servers vulnerable to CVE‑2026‑61500. The flaw allows session forgery, account takeover, and remote code execution.

items.title: Alleged ShinyHunters member reportedly detained in Jordan, assisting law enforcement
items.summary: Saif al‑Din Khader, alleged ShinyHunters member, was detained in Jordan and is cooperating with the FBI after a large breach exposed employee data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: FBI confirms 'multiple' arrests related to ShinyHunters hack
items.summary: The FBI announced several arrests related to the ShinyHunters hack, following the investigation into the data breach.

items.title: US, Australia warn of latest Citrix vulnerability after NetScaler advisory
items.summary: The United States and Australia warned about a new Citrix vulnerability affecting NetScaler deployments. Citrix said the issue is unrelated to recent problems.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: IQVIA fined $7.8 million for failing to properly anonymize health data
items.summary: Italy’s Data Protection Authority fined IQVIA €7 million ($7.8 million) for inadequate anonymization of health data that could expose about one million patients.

items.title: Ukraine grocery chain ATB confirms cyberattack as hackers threaten to leak data
items.summary: ATB, Ukraine’s largest grocery chain, confirmed a cyberattack after hackers posted an extortion demand on its website, threatening to leak data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft Exchange Flaw Lets Authenticated Attackers Read Other Users' Mailboxes
items.summary: Microsoft released out‑of‑band patches for a high‑severity flaw (CVE‑2026‑96940) in Exchange Server that allows authenticated attackers to elevate privileges and read other users’ mailboxes.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Impersonate US Officials for AI Cyber Espionage
items.summary: The threat group TA419 is impersonating U.S. officials and forging relationships with AI policy experts to facilitate cyber espionage.

items.title: Debian's latest kernel security update has 1,313 reasons to patch
items.summary: Debian’s latest kernel update includes 1,313 CVEs, driven by AI‑assisted bug hunting and expanded CVE rules that increase the number of vulnerabilities to patch.

items.title: University of Illinois Chicago affected by ransomware attack on medical school
items.summary: The University of Illinois Chicago College of Medicine suffered a ransomware attack that stole some server data.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Denmark population registry data breach affects 8.8 million people
items.summary: Denmark’s Central Population Register reported a breach exposing personal information of approximately 8.8 million residents.

items.title: Smashing the token limit with overlapping fragments
items.summary: A new technique allows attackers to exfiltrate larger tokens by overlapping fragments, expanding the amount of data that can be stolen.

items.title: CISA flags new exploited NetScaler flaw as attackers crash appliances (CVE-2026-88779)
items.summary: CISA added CVE‑2026‑88779, a memory‑overflow flaw in Citrix NetScaler, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; the bug can cause denial‑of‑service attacks on vulnerable appliances.

items.title: New Dell System Update flaw lets hackers gain root privileges
items.summary: Dell warned that a flaw in its System Update (DSU) CLI tool lets attackers gain root privileges, urging customers to patch immediately.

items.title: ClingSTUN Malware Turns Unpatched IoT Devices Into Proxy Nodes
items.summary: ClingSTUN malware exploits IoT device vulnerabilities and uses public STUN servers to turn unpatched devices into proxy nodes.

items.title: South Korea probes bank breaches amid suspected AI-powered attacks
items.summary: South Korea’s Financial Services Commission convened an emergency meeting after a series of cyberattacks targeted financial institutions. Investigations focus on suspected AI‑powered attack techniques. The commission is working to assess the scope and impact of the breaches.

items.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: NetScaler and FortiMail 0-Days, AI Coding Leaks, Spectre v2 and Ransomware Arrests
items.summary: The weekly recap covers actively exploited NetScaler and FortiMail zero‑days, AI code leaks, Spectre v2 vulnerabilities, and recent ransomware arrests. It highlights emerging threat vectors and the need for timely patching. The report underscores the evolving sophistication of attackers.

items.title: Fake brand discounts on social media prey on shoppers’ fear of missing out
items.summary: Cybercriminals are posting fake discount offers on Facebook and TikTok to lure shoppers to phishing sites that steal payment card details and OTPs. The Milk Dragon phishing kit has been active since October 2025, with 258 pages and victims in 66 countries. Group‑IB warns of the growing scale of this campaign.

items.title: LTM launches BlueVerse AgenTraceIQ to monitor AI agents and reverse unintended actions
items.summary:
LTM introduces BlueVerse AgenTraceIQ, combining Rubrik Agent Cloud with AI governance.
It monitors agentic AI, sets guardrails, and can rewind unintended actions in business‑critical environments.

items.title: tenfold CE: Our free Identity Governance tool just got 2 new features
items.summary:
tenfold adds shared content governance and real‑time event auditing to its free Community Edition.
The features help teams manage Microsoft 365 sharing and investigate suspicious identity activity.

items.title: Stellar Cyber 7.0 adds measurable workflows for AI-powered SOCs
items.summary:
Stellar Cyber releases version 7.0, adding AI‑powered case triage, measurable SOC workflows, deeper investigative evidence, and expanded automated response.
New APIs support scaling security operations.

items.title: Malwarebytes Scam Link Check analyzes URLs and explains potential risks
items.summary: Malwarebytes launched a free Scam Link Check tool that evaluates suspicious URLs and returns a safety rating. The tool explains the risks behind each link and recommends next steps. It is designed to help users avoid scams delivered via text, email, chat, or social media.

items.title: Citrix NetScaler Targeted Via New Zero Day
items.summary:
A memory buffer vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler can cause denial of service.
CISA warns it poses significant risks to federal government customers.

items.title: Japanese media group Nikkei discloses cyberattack targeting journalistic sources
items.summary:
Nikkei reports a cyber incident involving an employee email account that may have compromised journalistic sources.
The breach highlights potential loss of source confidentiality.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Alleged dev of Ploutus ATM malware appears in US court after arrest
items.summary: The U.S. DOJ arrests the alleged developer of Ploutus malware, used to steal millions in ATM jackpotting attacks across the United States.

items.title: Need for Speed: AI-Driven Attacks Are Changing Security Strategies
items.summary:
A Dark Reading poll shows AI‑powered attacks are fast, relentless, and automated.
Security teams are urged to adapt strategies to keep pace.

items.title: Linux Backdoor Abuses STUN Protocol, Exploits Dozens of Flaws
items.summary:
The ClingSTUN backdoor operates as a back‑connect proxy, establishes persistence, and exploits dozens of vulnerabilities through the STUN protocol.
It enables self‑propagation across Linux systems.

items.title: 250,000 Impacted by Data Breaches at New Jersey, Texas Healthcare Firms
items.summary:
Hackers stole patient data from Clover Health Investments and AngMar Management Services in July.
About 250,000 individuals in New Jersey and Texas were affected.

items.title: RemoveMacAI turns off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and deletes its models
items.summary:
RemoveMacAI is a free command‑line tool that disables Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and removes ~12 GB of AI models.
It is intended for Apple Silicon Macs where the feature cannot be turned off via settings.

items.title: Data breach at Denmark’s national population register exposes 8.8 million people
items.summary:
Denmark is investigating a data breach that exposed the personal data of approximately 8.8 million residents.
Unauthorized users accessed the national population register.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: The Credential Layer Is Expanding Faster Than Security Teams Can See It
items.summary:
The credential layer is growing faster than security teams can manage.
GitGuardian offers detection, remediation, and prevention to help organizations inventory and secure credentials.

items.title: Realtek Jungle SDK Exploit Attempts Deliver Cling Botnet With STUN-Based C2
items.summary:
Threat actors have targeted the Realtek Jungle SDK flaw to deploy the Cling botnet.
The malware uses STUN traffic as a command‑and‑control channel.

items.title: Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI
items.summary:
An AI model solved a cipher created in 1809 by Napoleon’s nephew.
The achievement demonstrates AI’s cryptanalysis capabilities.

items.title: Exploitation Hits Rejetto HFS Vulnerability Discovered by AI
items.summary:
CVE‑2026‑61500 in Rejetto HFS allows attackers to recover the session‑cookie signing key, gain administrative access, and execute remote code.
The vulnerability was discovered by AI.

items.title: Senate Passes Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Healthcare Cybersecurity
items.summary:
The U.S. Senate passed a bipartisan bill to strengthen cybersecurity in the healthcare sector.
Last year, 730 breaches affected 270 million Americans, averaging $10 million per incident.

items.title: Apple Plans Tighter macOS Full Disk Access Controls Over AI Agent Data Access
items.summary:
Apple announced tighter controls for macOS Full Disk Access to mitigate risks posed by AI agents.
The changes aim to prevent developers from exposing users’ files, mail, messages, and browsing history.

items.title: Out-of-band Exchange Server update fixes high-severity mailbox access bug (CVE-2026-96940)
items.summary:
Microsoft released an out‑of‑band update for Exchange Server that fixes CVE‑2026‑96940.
The vulnerability could let authenticated attackers read other users’ emails and attachments within the same tenant.

items.title: Detained ShinyHunters hacker reportedly helping FBI track down fellow members
items.summary:
Jordanian authorities detained a suspected ShinyHunters member known as Rey.
He is cooperating with the FBI by reviewing his electronic devices to locate other group members.

items.title: Google Suspends Open-Source Bug Bounty Due to AI Vulnerability Reports
items.summary:
Google paused its Open Source Vulnerability Rewards Program after a surge of AI‑generated vulnerability reports.
The pause follows concerns about the quality and volume of submissions.

items.title: OpenAI will show visual ads in ChatGPT while you generate images
items.summary: OpenAI is adding visual advertisements to ChatGPT. The new format will display ads while users generate images.

items.title: The US needs a real plan to defend its water systems
items.summary: The United States needs a comprehensive plan to protect water systems. This includes stronger defenses for large utilities, hands‑on support for smaller systems, and federal backing.

items.title: MAKERphone 2: A DIY 4G phone with plug-in camera, speaker and prototyping board
items.summary: CircuitMess is selling the MAKERphone 2.0, a DIY 4G phone. It can be programmed in MicroPython or Arduino C++ and expanded with plug‑in camera, speaker, and prototyping board modules.

items.title: Microsoft: Windows KB5124010 update crashes some games and apps
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that the KB5124010 Windows 11 preview update causes crashes in games and applications that use AC‑3 Dolby Digital audio decoding.

items.title: More UK Schools Are Recovering Faster from Cyber Incidents
items.summary: An Ofqual study found that more UK schools are recovering immediately from cyber incidents. The trend indicates faster resilience to attacks.

items.title: Legacy sign-on service comes back to bite school software provider Bromcom
items.summary: Intruders accessed email addresses from a legacy sign‑on service still running for an internal system at Bromcom. The breach exposed sensitive user data. The incident highlights the risks of maintaining outdated authentication services.

items.title: Frontline Education Breach Impacts K-12 School District Staff
items.summary: A breach at Frontline Education exposed employee data of K‑12 school district staff. The incident impacted staff information security.

items.title: Apple tightens macOS disk access as AI agents become more powerful
items.summary: Apple will introduce stricter Full Disk Access controls in macOS. Users must explicitly grant permission as AI agents become more powerful.

items.title: Attackers Target Rejetto HFS Flaw That Enables Admin Session Forgery and RCE
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE‑2026‑61500 in Rejetto HTTP File Server. The flaw allows session forgery and can lead to remote code execution.

items.title: doxx.net opens Agentic Defined Networking public beta, raises $38 million
items.summary: doxx.net launched a public beta of its Agentic Defined Networking platform. The service enables private, server‑less networks for agents and raised $38 million in funding.

items.title: AI slop submissions force Google to freeze its open-source bug bounty
items.summary: Google has stopped accepting new submissions to its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program. The halt follows a wave of invalid AI‑generated reports.

items.title: Alleged ShinyHunters Leader Arrested in Jordan
items.summary: Jordan authorities arrested an individual known as Rey, alleged leader of the ShinyHunters extortion group. The suspect is cooperating with the FBI to identify and locate other members.

items.title: New NetScaler Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks Can Knock SAML Deployments Offline
items.summary: Citrix released security updates for CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow flaw in NetScaler ADC and Gateway. The vulnerability, scored 8.7/10, has been exploited in targeted attacks that can bring SAML deployments offline.

items.title: Three questions a hospital CISO should ask a healthcare fintech vendor
items.summary: In an interview, Drew McCombs, CTO and CISO at Cylerity, discussed how security is integrated into every sprint. He explained measures to keep PHI separate from banking partners, the role of AI recommendations, and the importance of MFA for email.

items.title: Exploitation of Citrix NetScaler Zero-Day Hits Appliances Patched Days Earlier
items.summary: Citrix confirmed that CVE-2026-88779 was exploited shortly after two other vulnerabilities were patched. The zero‑day attack occurred just days after the patches were released.

items.title: Citrix patches NetScaler SAML zero-day exploited in attacks
items.summary: Citrix issued emergency patches for a denial‑of‑service vulnerability, CVE-2026-88779, that has been used in zero‑day attacks. Researchers are investigating whether the flaw can also enable remote code execution.

items.title: Trump Names National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton to Lead a New Federal AI Task Force
items.summary:
President Trump appointed National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton to head a new federal AI task force.
The decision follows a White House meeting with AI company executives.
Reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Anthropic asks Claude users to share voice data for AI model training
items.summary: Anthropic has requested Claude users to voluntarily share voice conversations to train its AI models, with participation remaining optional.

items.title: Week in review: Researcher breaks into Microsoft analytics service, NetScaler RCE 0-day exploited
items.summary: A 16‑year‑old researcher exposed a flaw in Microsoft’s internal analytics service, Titan, that could allow reading of employee records and Bing search data; the same week also saw exploitation of a NetScaler RCE zero‑day.

items.title: ShinyHunters Suspect Rey Reportedly Detained in Jordan, Helping FBI Identify Group Members
items.summary: A suspected ShinyHunters member, alias Rey (Saif al‑Din Khader), was reportedly detained in Jordan on September 29, 2026, and is said to have cooperated with the FBI to identify other group members.

items.title: China-Aligned TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts With Microsoft AitM Phishing
items.summary: TA419, a China‑aligned espionage group, carried out credential phishing campaigns against U.S. AI experts in think tanks, universities, and legal sectors, impersonating prominent economists, AI policymakers, and an Anthropic employee.

items.title: Google Gemini could soon get full access to your Mac’s files, apps and the web
items.summary: Google’s Gemini AI may soon be granted unrestricted access to macOS files, applications, and web browsing, potentially bypassing permission prompts and allowing the model to perform actions without user confirmation.
